stem: P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.3, and P(A and B) = 0.12. Find P(A | B).

per_option_rationale.rationale: Returning P(B) = 0.3, confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A) or simply reading the wrong value from the given data.
Returning P(A and B) = 0.12 directly without dividing by P(B), solving for the joint probability instead of the conditional.
Computing P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) = 0.4 + 0.3 - 0.12 = 0.58... actually applying union formula, or misadding 0.4 + 0.12 = 0.52.

explanation: The conditional probability formula is P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B). Substituting: 0.12 / 0.3 = 0.4. Notice this equals P(A), which is consistent with A and B being independent (0.4 x 0.3 = 0.12).

explanation_sections.punchline: P(A|B) divides the joint probability by the conditioning event's probability.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: conditional probability definition. Given: P(A and B)=0.12, P(B)=0.3. Apply P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B) = 0.12/0.3 = 0.4.
explanation_sections.lesson: P(A|B) is always the joint probability divided by the probability of the event being conditioned on.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Read the formula, substitute, divide. The trap is returning P(B) or P(A and B) directly.
